title: Redirection [stderr, 2>]
description:
# Standard Streams
Every program has three streams:
- `stdin` (0) - input
- `stdout` (1) - normal output
- `stderr` (2) - error output

`>` only redirects stdout. Errors still show on screen:
```bash
ls /fake > output.txt
# error still prints to terminal!
```

## Redirecting stderr:
```bash
ls /fake 2> errors.txt       # stderr to file
ls /fake > out.txt 2>&1       # both stdout AND stderr to file
ls /fake 2>/dev/null          # throw away errors
```

`2>` means redirect stream 2 (stderr).
`2>&1` means redirect stderr to wherever stdout goes.
`/dev/null` is a black hole - anything sent there disappears.
